correctness.rationale: Weight-one differences with nonzero f-image force associated parity rows of weight>=3; weight-two differences with distinct nonzero images force parity-row pair distance>=2. Fix one parity coordinate: hypercube matching pairs by its toggle have 2^(r-1) pairs, of which exactly r (prefix weights 0 or 1) have both endpoints weight<=2, hence <=2^(r-1)-r selected rows; this lower bound is sharp by assigning distinct odd-weight rows of weight>=3. For x with wt<=3 and f(x)!=0, 1,2,3 selected nonzero rows give nonzero parity in the necessary cases (three odd-weight rows have odd XOR; two distinct labels do not cancel). For larger x, systematic weight >=4. The proof treats zero/repeated images and empty function. Independent small-dimensional exhaustive parity testing found no violation; finite cases complement the uniform algebraic proof.

value.rationale: This determines an entire natural binary systematic function-correction problem at the first separation beyond earlier studied distances, including functions with kernels, zeros and repeated nonzero image columns. The ν invariant is an unexpectedly complete reduction from a global family of protected-message constraints to one discrete count; the tight matching construction is independently useful for systematic code design.

final_claim: For binary linear f with ν distinct nonzero images of the distinguished basis, exact linear-systematic redundancy to separate unequal f-values at Hamming distance 4 is 0 for ν=0, otherwise the least r>=3 satisfying ν<=2^(r-1)-r; for all nonzero columns of F2^s it equals s+2.
limitations: Binary linear f and binary LINEAR systematic encoders with designated message basis, at distance exactly four.
